The beginning goes way back to the days of the westward expansion of the white people into the west. The majority of the BLM land of course belonged to the Native Americans, but was 'given' to the US government by way of treaty. Fast forward past the era of homesteading, the lands that were not homesteaded on cause they were too barren/remote for farming were essentially kept by the government as a 'public trust' and the BLM was created to manage it for the benefit of all. And most people don't know but some of the lands were privately owned (by people like the Hammond family) but the areas they owned were so large that they ended up actually giving it to the BLM cause the taxes to be paid on it were much higher than they could ever get in revenue from grazing it.

The problem is the BLM (like quite a few government agencies) has a lot of power over people, but no clear rules governing how things are actually done. Early on before the BLM came about, the lands were being leased to the ranchers that lived in the areas cause even though you can't farm it, you can raise cattle on it since they can efficiently graze over long distances. East coast politicians and farmers took offense at the relatively low price the government was leasing the rights for since they never really appreciated how barren the land really is compared to their own lands. Suffice to say they always pushed to have the grazing fees raised. And now, the BLM basically has one real directive from the Congress who controls its budget: Make money so we don't have to give it to you. And they are doing just that in many ways, some of them good, some of them not.

Now, in the most recent years, the technology and need for energy and rare metals has skyrocketed, so the BLM, whose controllers have deeper roots in DC then the west, are signing major deals with mining and energy firms to harvest resources. These deals are big money, far more than what the BLM makes off of the grazing rights.

So, does this completely explain why the ranchers are completely angry to the point of risking their lives? Not completely, there is admittedly some grey areas here, but they are very serious grey areas.

Basically, the BLM has been growing more and more hostile to the ranchers by either completely kicking them off lands or raising rates beyond what is sustainable for the ranchers. The reasons are varied and sometimes highly circumspect. They often are for 'environmental reasons' or just plain unexplained.

The case in Oregon goes beyond reason in the areas of shadiness. The whole trial was a farce (coerced witnesses, etc.) And the biggest kicker of all is that the BLM is basically the law in court, meaning they control the rules and are the prosecutor and police.

The tactics used by BLM are especially heinous. The Hammonds were charged for two fires set a long time ago under terrorism laws. Terrorism. For a fire. The first fire caused no problems (actually a typical controlled burn to prevent huge fires) and the second was to save land from a fire. So they were prosecuted for not actually doing anything wrong. The judge thought the minimum sentence was ridiculous so he lowered it. Then after they served their time some other person thought that wasn't enough and resentenced them to serve the minimum sentence. In addition, there's a lien on the property so that they can only sell it to BLM.

While the Hammonds weren't the only reason, I suspect BLM is behind the reason beef prices have been rising lately because of tactics like this against all ranchers.
